title: Cloud-commanded dock return observed over BLE -- the feed cadence is a link property, not a motion-pattern artifact
motion_source: mower own autonomous navigation, dock return commanded from the phone app over CLOUD; integration stayed on BLE

sampling.note: Sampled ~3x faster than the feed so the sampler interval cannot be mistaken for the feed rate -- the confound that invalidated an earlier measurement.

key_findings: Feed cadence during the mower OWN continuous autonomous navigation is median 1.15 s -- statistically the same as the 1031 ms measured during our pulsed motion. The ~1 s cadence is a property of the device/link, NOT an artifact of how we drive.
Median 29.3 cm and max 59.2 cm of travel between position updates. Mammotion own dock-return navigation is positionally blind for ~30 cm at a time.
This independently justifies waypoint_tolerance 0.15: the vendor own navigation does not have finer feedback than this, so expecting 8 cm waypoint accuracy was never realistic on this hardware.
Speed median 0.285 m/s matches our fast tier (0.207-0.322), so the comparison is like-for-like.
Steps are strikingly consistent (0.284-0.310 m for 10 of 14), suggesting a fixed internal control interval rather than jitter.
One 14.67 s gap mid-drive with a following 0.592 m step (2x the median) -- a dropped update, consistent with a brief BLE stall at self-reported -74 to -76 dBm.
caveat: ble_rssi values quoted here are the MOWER self-report (report_data.connect.ble_rssi), not the advertisement RSSI that gates BLETransport.is_usable (min_rssi = -90). The gating value is not surfaced anywhere in this integration.
